subject: Targeted route anchoring ask for Keystone pilot (no-fallback)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Keystone Health <security@keystone.health>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Targeted route anchoring ask for Keystone pilot (no-fallback)

Hi team —

Quick context: Keystone's pilot starts next week and their legal/compliance team is requesting a strict routing binding for the pilot traffic (US-only) with no automatic fallback to other variants/models. They want a single pinned model variant and a region lock for the pilot dataset due to regulatory concerns around PHI-handling and data residency.

Ask: can we provision a short-lived targeted route anchoring policy for this pilot (14 days) that: 
- pins requests from keystone.health/* to model: rwx-1.3-us-hp (exact variant)
- enforces region: us-east-1 only
- disables automatic fallback to cheaper or multi-region variants

Why: Keystone says even a brief fallback to a non-US variant is a contractual no-go. We agreed to the pilot on the premise of demonstrating latency and cost; the customer accepts higher per-token cost for the pilot but requires proof that traffic will never egress to non-US variants.

Attached: keystone_soc2_summary.pdf (high-level extract they sent) and a draft runbook for anchor revocation.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev: confirm technical feasibility and rollback plan if the anchored node has an outage (can we fail closed?)
2) Marcus: estimate incremental cost impact and monitoring hooks we should enable
3) Lauren: if product/legal OK, escalate to InfoSec for signoff by EOD Mon

Can we treat this as an exception (pilot-only) and have an automated expiry so ops isn't left owning a permanent hardlock?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Keystone Health <security@keystone.health>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted route anchoring ask for Keystone pilot (no-fallback)

Jasmine —

Thanks for the quick note. We appreciate the compromise on cost. A few clarifying questions before we sign off on anything: 
1) Are you able to provide an auditable proof that no fallback occurred (logs/traces) for every request? We need per-request region/model attribution in the event of an audit.
2) If you "fail closed" and the US anchor becomes unavailable, will traffic be blocked entirely or queued until restoration? We need guaranteed non-ejection; blocking temporarily is acceptable only if we can present a mitigation to impacted internal users.
3) What is the change window and how will rollback be executed (DocuSign or signed change request)?

Also attached is our minimal evidence ask: can you confirm SOC2 controls mapping to ingestion/processing?

— Sarah K.
Security Program Manager
Keystone Health
security@keystone.health

Subject: Re: Targeted route anchoring ask for Keystone pilot (no-fallback)

Hey all —

Short answers up front: technically feasible with caveats; we can implement a short-lived route anchor that pins a route to a specific model variant and region and disables automatic fallback. Implementation notes: 
- We will create a per-account routing policy (scope: keystone.health) with explicit model_variant_id and region_id.
- Logging: every request will be recorded with model_variant, host_region, and selected_node_id. We can provide daily exported logs to Keystone (S3 link with ACL) for the pilot duration. That satisfies the per-request attribution ask.
- Failure mode: to meet their "no egress" requirement we must "fail closed" — i.e., return 503 when the anchored variant is unavailable. We can implement a short retry/backoff window (30s) before returning 503. No automatic ejection to other variants.

Risks and mitigations: 
- If the anchored fleet has an infrastructure outage, customer-facing traffic will degrade. Mitigation: we propose a secondary manual-runbook failover that switches the anchor to an accredited standby node in the same region (manual approval required, documented in the runbook). That keeps control with Keystone/legal.
- Monitoring: we will enable an Ops dashboard and alert channel; Marcus please advise SLO/alert thresholds.

Cost: Marcus, please provide delta. My rough ballpark is +18-35% per-token depending on node sizing since we won't use multi-region pooling.

I attached a draft runbook (route_anchor_runbook.md) with steps for provisioning, monitoring, and manual failover.

Happy to stand up a 30-min tech sync today if useful.

— Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
